question: The Feroz Shah Kotla Fort, also known as the home of the djinns, was built in __________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**1354**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• **Feroz Shah Kotla Fort** was built in the year **1354** by **Feroz Shah Tughlaq**, the Sultan of the Delhi Sultanate. 
• It was constructed as the capital of his new city named **Firozabad**, which was the fifth city of Delhi. 
• The fort is known for its unique architecture, including a prominent **Ashokan Pillar** brought from Ambala and placed on top of the fort. 
• It is locally referred to as the **"home of the djinns"**, as it is believed by locals that spirits or djinns inhabit the ruins. 
• The fort reflects the architectural style of the **Tughlaq dynasty**, known for its simplicity and use of local resources like quartzite stone. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Feroz Shah Tughlaq:** 
• He was the third ruler of the **Tughlaq dynasty** and ruled from **1351 to 1388**. 
• He is known for his administrative reforms, including the introduction of **irrigation canals** and the construction of new cities like Firozabad. 
• He shifted the capital from Tughlaqabad to **Firozabad**. 
• **Ashokan Pillar:** 
• The fort houses one of the **Ashokan Pillars**, which was transported from Topra (Haryana) to Delhi under the direction of Feroz Shah Tughlaq. 
• The pillar is inscribed with edicts of Emperor Ashoka, dating back to the **3rd century BCE**. 
• **Architectural Features:** 
• The fort comprises a **pyramid-shaped structure** to support the Ashokan Pillar. 
• It also includes a **Jami Masjid** (mosque), one of the largest mosques in Delhi during that time. 
• The architecture primarily used **quartzite stone**, reflecting the simple yet robust style of the Tughlaq dynasty. 
• **Historical Significance:** 
• The fort served as the capital of the Delhi Sultanate under Feroz Shah Tughlaq. 
• It played a crucial role in the administration and defense of the empire during the 14th century. 
• **Local Beliefs:** 
• The fort is associated with **supernatural folklore**, where locals believe that djinns inhabit its ruins. 
• Even today, people visit the fort to offer letters and prayers to the djinns, seeking blessings and solutions to their problems. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Tughlaq Dynasty:** The Tughlaq dynasty was a prominent ruling dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate, known for its administrative reforms and architectural achievements. 
• **Firozabad:** The city of Firozabad, established by Feroz Shah Tughlaq, was one of the seven historic cities of Delhi. 
• **Preservation:** Although in ruins today, the Feroz Shah Kotla Fort is maintained by the **Archaeological Survey of India (ASI)**, highlighting its cultural and historical importance. 
• **Tourism:** The fort is a popular tourist attraction, offering insights into the Tughlaq era's history and architecture. </ul
